text:
If you’re hoping to get outside today, give the morning clouds a little time and expect a brighter, cooler afternoon, with a high right around 72. A north wind at 7 to 12 mph will keep it feeling fresh, and the lake will be the roughest early, with winds around 15 to 20 knots and waves up to 2 feet before easing. It’s a good day for a walk or a short outing, but I’d be cautious about heading onto open water first thing. Tonight stays mostly clear, with just a slight chance of a shower around 9 or 10.

Labor Day looks warmer and sunnier, near 78, with light winds and much calmer water. The forecasters’ own discussion keeps us mostly dry through Tuesday, but a much wetter stretch is expected Wednesday night into Thursday morning. Plan on the lake settling down this evening, and take advantage of the best outdoor window from late morning through the afternoon.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - A trough will bring showers tonight, mainly from the Champlain Valley and areas to the east. It will be a cooler night with lows ranging from the mid-40s to mid-50s. A few showers may linger into very early Sunday morning. Otherwise, the rest of the day will be mostly sunny and pleasant with highs in the upper 60s to low 70s. It will be great for the last day of the Champlain Valley Fair. High pressure will keep the sunshine around for Labor Day as well. Expect warmer highs in the mid to upper 70s.
